result.topic_en: This is the opening of Euler's paper on testing whether large numbers are prime: if N can be written as aa + λbb in two different ways, then N is composite and its factors can be found.
result.transcription:
[Left-hand page (p. 10), end of the preceding piece: a table of values of $a$, from 1 to 299, for which a quadratic formula ($3?aa+1$ [?]) gives primes, ending 'horum numerorum ultimi fere ad 20 milliones exsurgunt.']

11
METHODUS GENERALIOR
NUMEROS QUOSVIS SATIS GRANDES PERSCRUTANDI
UTRUM SINT PRIMI NEC NE?
AUCTORE
L. EULERO.
Conventui exhibita die 16 Martii 1778.

§. 1.
Sit N numerus propositus, et non difficile erit eum reducere ad hujusmodi formam: $N = aa + \lambda bb$; tum vero inquiratur, utrum adhuc alio modo ad similem formam reduci queat. Si enim quoque fuerit $N = xx + \lambda yy$, ita ut sit $aa + \lambda bb = xx + \lambda yy$, tum certe numerus N non erit primus, sed ejus factores hoc modo assignari poterunt. Quoniam hinc est $aa - xx = \lambda(yy - bb)$, erit $\frac{a+x}{y+b} = \lambda \cdot \frac{y-b}{a-x}$, quae fractiones ad minimos terminos reducti sint $\lambda \cdot \frac{p}{q}$. Ponatur igitur $a + x = \lambda mp$ et $y - b = np$, erit $y + b = mq$ et $a - x = nq$, et hinc reperietur $a = \frac{\lambda mp + nq}{2}$ et $b = \frac{mq - np}{2}$, ex quibus valoribus, erit $N = \frac{1}{4}(\lambda mm + nn)(\lambda pp + qq)$; unde patet, formulam $\lambda pp + qq$ vel ipsam, vel ejus semissem, vel quadrantem esse factorem numeri propositi N.

§. 2. Quando autem ad talem formam $N = aa + \lambda bb$ pervenimus, tum statuamus $N = xx + \lambda yy$, ubi statim facile patebit, utrum hi numeri $x$ et $y$ sint pares, an vero impares, quo reperto statuatur vel $N - \lambda yy = xx$, vel $N - xx = \lambda yy$; ac priori quidem casu numerus $x$ ita accipi

items.english: A more general method of examining any sufficiently large numbers to determine whether they are prime or not.

items.quote: Sit N numerus propositus, et non difficile erit eum reducere ad hujusmodi formam: $N = aa + \lambda bb$; tum vero inquiratur, utrum adhuc alio modo ad similem formam reduci queat.
items.english: Let N be the proposed number. It will not be difficult to reduce it to the form N = aa + λbb. Then one should investigate whether it can be reduced to a similar form in yet another way.

items.quote: Si enim quoque fuerit $N = xx + \lambda yy$, ita ut sit $aa + \lambda bb = xx + \lambda yy$, tum certe numerus N non erit primus, sed ejus factores hoc modo assignari poterunt.
items.english: For if also N = xx + λyy, so that aa + λbb = xx + λyy, then the number N will certainly not be prime, and its factors can be assigned in the following way.

items.quote: erit $N = \frac{1}{4}(\lambda mm + nn)(\lambda pp + qq)$; unde patet, formulam $\lambda pp + qq$ vel ipsam, vel ejus semissem, vel quadrantem esse factorem numeri propositi N.
items.english: N = ¼(λmm + nn)(λpp + qq). Hence it is evident that the formula λpp + qq, or its half, or its quarter, is a factor of the proposed number N.

items.quote: Quando autem ad talem formam $N = aa + \lambda bb$ pervenimus, tum statuamus $N = xx + \lambda yy$, ubi statim facile patebit, utrum hi numeri $x$ et $y$ sint pares, an vero impares, quo reperto statuatur vel $N - \lambda yy = xx$, vel $N - xx = \lambda yy$
items.english: When we have arrived at such a form N = aa + λbb, let us set N = xx + λyy. It will at once be easily evident whether these numbers x and y are even or odd. Once this is found, set either N − λyy = xx or N − xx = λyy.
